title: Furrowed tree bark
purpose: Generate tileable PBR maps of tree bark with the trunk axis along the tile height: plates and furrows, interlaced ridges or stringy fibres, with cross-checks, lichen and moss. Use on tree trunks, logs and wooden props.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python bark_furrowed.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.meaning: Bark structure: 0 plates, 1 interlaced ridges, 2 stringy fibres.

parameters.name: ridges_across
parameters.meaning: Plates or ridges across the tile width.

parameters.name: plate_length
parameters.meaning: Plate rows down the tile (fewer rows give longer plates).

parameters.name: furrow_depth
parameters.meaning: Depth of the furrows between plates or ridges.

parameters.name: furrow_width
parameters.meaning: Width of the furrows, in plate widths.

parameters.name: flakes
parameters.meaning: Layered flaking inside the plates: stepped rims parallel to the plate edge.

parameters.name: lichen
parameters.meaning: Pale lichen patches on the plates.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Grey-brown oak-like plates with deep furrows and some lichen.

presets.name: pine_plates
presets.description: Reddish pine plates with dark furrows and flaky checks.

presets.name: ash_ridges
presets.description: Grey interlaced ridges in a diamond net.

presets.name: cedar_stringy
presets.description: Red-brown stringy fibres in long strips.

presets.name: mossy_old
presets.description: Old dark bark with moss filling the furrows.

limits: Three stylized bark structures from noise and Voronoi cells; species are suggested by colour and proportion, not reproduced. The texture assumes a cylinder unwrapped along its axis, so it does not taper or bend around branches. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate.
technique_references: Anisotropic Worley cells for bark plates
Ridged fractal noise stretched along the trunk for interlaced ridges
Domain warping with nearest-pixel warping of cell ids
Terraced flaking from quantized border distance
Height to tangent-space normal by central differences
